title: A Passage for the Compass
premise: Edmund Joubert, a riverboat captain haunted by a debt to the family that once financed her boat, is hired to find the missing Halvorsen expedition upriver. The trail leads through drowned villages, a smuggler's toll, and a pass that closes with the snows. Edmund discovers the expedition's leader is the son of her creditor, carrying letters that rewrite what she remembers of her own past. Betrayed by the expedition's financier, who wants the mountains' secret kept, Edmund must choose between reclaiming her boat and saving her found crew. Crossing the range ahead of the snows and outrunning the monsoon, she delivers the truth, forgives the debt, and returns downriver with a family she chose and a compass that finally points somewhere she wants to go.
about_author: Hazel Sandoval is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons working commercial routes in remote delta country before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who belong more to water and weather than to any one place.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Sandbar
chapters.summary: Edmund Joubert pilots her aging riverboat through low-water season, reading currents by instinct. A debt collector's letter waits at the dock. POV: Edmund. Beat: establish her competence, isolation, and the quiet dread of the debt that owns her boat.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: A survey office hires Edmund to investigate the Halvorsen expedition, silent for eleven days upriver. The pay would clear half her debt. She refuses, then finds the expedition's advance payment already credited to her account by mistake. POV: Edmund. Beat: reluctant hook; fate disguised as clerical error.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Edmund takes on three travelers: Ines, the expedition's cartographer; Tomas, a teenage stowaway claiming kinship with the missing party; and Mr. Vane, a polite financier's agent with too many questions. POV: Edmund. Beat: found-family seeds planted among strangers with secrets.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: They pass a village half-swallowed by the reservoir, where an old woman recognizes Edmund's compass and calls it by a name she doesn't know. POV: Edmund. Beat: first crack in her certainty about her own past; memory as unreliable cargo.

chapters.title: First Sign
chapters.summary: At a trading post, they find the expedition's abandoned supply cache, opened carefully, not looted. Ines reads the trail marks: the party went inland voluntarily. Tomas recognizes his uncle's knotwork. POV: Ines. Beat: hope sharpened into purpose; the mystery gains a shape.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: A river gang demands passage payment Edmund cannot make. Vane quietly settles it, revealing he carries more money than an agent should. POV: Tomas. Beat: distrust of Vane deepens; Tomas sees what the adults miss.

chapters.title: Night Currents
chapters.summary: Running the river after dark to escape the gang, Edmund nearly wrecks on a hidden bar and is saved by Ines's star fixes. The two women trade fragments of their pasts. POV: Edmund. Beat: intimacy through shared danger; trust begins.

chapters.title: What the Compass Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund examines the compass, engraved with initials that match the old woman's story: it belonged to the Halvorsen patriarch, who financed her boat years ago. The debt and the compass are the same inheritance. POV: Edmund. Beat: identity destabilized; her whole life recontextualized.

chapters.title: The Last Landing
chapters.summary: The river becomes unnavigable. They hire mules and a taciturn guide, Sefu, who knows the mountain trails. Vane objects to the route, insisting on a longer southern pass. POV: Sefu. Beat: new landscape, new rules; Vane's agenda surfaces.

chapters.title: Footprints in the Ash
chapters.summary: Following an old burn line, they find the expedition's camp: abandoned in order, with a journal page describing a valley the maps omit. Tomas finds his uncle's hat. POV: Ines. Beat: grief and resolve; the missing are alive by choice.

chapters.title: Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas catches Vane radioing their position to someone downriver. Confronted, Vane claims he's protecting an investment: his employer funded the expedition and wants its findings controlled. POV: Tomas. Beat: betrayal revealed; the crew must decide to continue without him.

chapters.title: Leaving Vane
chapters.summary: They strand Vane at a mission station with supplies and a lie about their route. Edmund feels the debt's weight differently now: some obligations are traps. POV: Edmund. Beat: moral turning point; loyalty to the crew over the contract.

chapters.title: The Ascent Begins
chapters.summary: The trail climbs out of the river basin. Sefu warns the high pass closes with early snow, and the monsoon is late and heavy behind them. POV: Ines. Beat: the race against two weathers is set; wonder and dread.

chapters.title: Cloud Forest
chapters.summary: In dripping forest, they find a carved marker in a language Sefu half-knows: a warning about the valley. Ines sketches it. That night Edmund dreams of her childhood on this river. POV: Edmund. Beat: memory and myth braiding together.

chapters.title: The Broken Bridge
chapters.summary: A storm-swollen gorge has taken the rope bridge. Sefu leads a traverse along the cliff; Tomas freezes halfway and Edmund talks him across, hand over hand. POV: Tomas. Beat: fear conquered; Tomas stops being a stowaway and becomes crew.

chapters.title: Letters from the Dead
chapters.summary: In a cairn, they find mail the expedition cached: letters home, including one to Edmund's creditor from his son, Daniel Halvorsen, the expedition's leader, writing about a valley that 'remembers people.' POV: Ines. Beat: the personal and the quest converge.

chapters.title: The Valley the Maps Omit
chapters.summary: They crest a ridge and see it: a hidden valley with terraced ruins and smoke from inhabited fires. The expedition didn't vanish; it stayed. POV: Edmund. Beat: awe; the answer arrives before the understanding.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: They meet the expedition, healthy, secretive, led by Daniel Halvorsen. Tomas embraces his uncle. Daniel recognizes Edmund and the compass, and goes pale. POV: Daniel. Beat: joy undercut by guilt; Daniel knows what the compass means.

chapters.title: What They Found
chapters.summary: Daniel explains: the valley holds an archive of the river's original peoples, and proof that the reservoir project Edmund's creditor financed drowned a living culture knowingly. The expedition stayed to document it before the evidence is flooded again. POV: Daniel. Beat: the debt's true nature revealed; her boat was bought with complicity.

chapters.title: The Choice of Staying
chapters.summary: Daniel asks them to stay through winter and help finish the record. Edmund refuses: the monsoon will cut the river, stranding the valley people without supplies. Someone must go back. POV: Edmund. Beat: duty versus discovery; she chooses the people over the prize.

chapters.title: Sefu's Warning
chapters.summary: Sefu reads the sky: the pass will hold maybe four more days. Staying longer means a winter in the valley. The expedition splits over whether to trust Edmund's urgency. POV: Sefu. Beat: ticking clock made flesh; leadership tested.

chapters.title: Vane Returns
chapters.summary: Vane arrives with hired men, having tracked them. He offers Daniel a fortune to surrender the archive, and threatens to have the valley 'surveyed' out of existence. POV: Daniel. Beat: antagonist closes in; money against memory.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns
chapters.summary: A fire, set by one of Vane's men, consumes half the archive. Ines and the expedition's scholars salvage what they can, copying fragments through the night. POV: Ines. Beat: devastating loss; grief transmuted into urgency to carry the truth out.

chapters.title: Edmund's Bargain
chapters.summary: Edmund confronts Vane: she'll testify that his employer knew the reservoir would destroy the valley, unless he lets them leave with the copies. Vane calls her bluff, revealing he holds her debt paper. POV: Edmund. Beat: stakes made personal; her freedom is the ransom.

chapters.title: The Debt Burned
chapters.summary: Daniel produces his father's letters: the debt was forgiven years ago; Vane has been collecting illegally. Edmund burns the paper herself. POV: Edmund. Beat: liberation; she was never owned, only deceived.

chapters.title: Flight from the Valley
chapters.summary: With copies of the archive, the expedition's core, and valley guides, they race for the pass as Vane's men pursue. Snow dusts the high trail. POV: Tomas. Beat: full flight; the chase is on.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Vane's men block the narrows. Sefu's route knowledge lets them climb a goat path instead, but the valley's eldest guide falls and is carried, slowing them. POV: Sefu. Beat: cost of escape; no one left behind.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: The snows arrive early. In whiteout, Edmund navigates by the compass and by memory of her father's stories of this pass, discovering he crossed it once himself, with Halvorsen. POV: Edmund. Beat: inheritance reclaimed; her past becomes her instrument.

chapters.title: The Eldest's Story
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a cave, the valley's eldest tells the story the archive holds: how the river people were promised, and betrayed, by the same men Edmund's world called benefactors. POV: the eldest. Beat: theme crystallized; memory is the treasure.

chapters.title: Tomas's Turn
chapters.summary: Tomas carries the eldest over the worst scree when the guides falter, proving himself. His uncle sees him clearly for the first time. POV: Tomas. Beat: coming of age; the boy becomes the man who carries others.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Gamble
chapters.summary: Vane, half-frozen and abandoned by his hired men, stumbles into their camp. Edmund could leave him. She doesn't. He breaks, confessing his employer ordered the archive fire. POV: Edmund. Beat: mercy as strength; the antagonist disarmed by grace.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Below the snowline, the air turns warm and wet: the monsoon's edge. They descend through rising rivers as the mountain gives way to green. POV: Ines. Beat: relief laced with new urgency; the river is rising behind them.

chapters.title: The Boat Waits
chapters.summary: They reach the river to find Edmund's boat looted but afloat, guarded by the mission sisters she once ferried for free. Kindness returns as rescue. POV: Edmund. Beat: grace repaid; the world is not only debts.

chapters.title: Running the Flood
chapters.summary: Edmund pilots the overloaded boat down the monsoon-swollen river through three days and nights of flood, the crew working as one. POV: Edmund. Beat: climax of skill; every lesson of the journey pays off at once.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: In the river city, they deliver the archive copies to a judge and a newspaper. Vane, testifying under immunity, confirms his employer's knowledge. The reservoir's expansion is suspended. POV: Daniel. Beat: justice without triumphalism; truth does its slow work.

chapters.title: What Edmund Owes
chapters.summary: Debt-free, Edmund is offered a commission to run supply routes to the valley. She realizes she no longer knows who she is without the debt. Daniel tells her the compass was always meant for her. POV: Edmund. Beat: identity rebuilt; freedom is heavier than debt.

chapters.title: The Naming
chapters.summary: Tomas formally joins the expedition as an apprentice; Ines takes a post mapping the valley properly; Sefu becomes their guide of record. Edmund realizes her crew has become her family. POV: Tomas. Beat: found family sealed in small ceremonies.

chapters.title: The Valley Opens
chapters.summary: Edmund carries the first supply run up the reopened route, the expedition's scholars riding her deck. The valley people greet the boat with songs the old woman from the drowned village once knew. POV: Edmund. Beat: reconciliation; the drowned and the living joined.

chapters.title: Compass Reading
chapters.summary: Edmund opens the compass and finds, beneath the plate Daniel repaired, her father's initials beside Halvorsen's: the two families were partners once, before the debt and the dam divided them. POV: Edmund. Beat: final revelation; memory restored, identity made whole.

chapters.title: A Passage for the Compass
chapters.summary: Edmund stands at the wheel as the river carries her down toward the delta, her crew around her, the monsoon behind and the mountains ahead holding the valley's memory safe. She is no one's debtor and someone's family. POV: Edmund. Beat: resolution; the passage was never just upriver, but home.
